description:
FILED s484a (Opus, 2026-09-13) from the #1628 probe battery
(scratch/s484a/probes/g1628.pl, 17 rows).  PRE-EXISTING: every row below is
byte-identical on main 2ffefb36 and on the s484a tree -- #1628's fix is the
box-referent rule and does not reach a typeglob referent.

perl draws a line PCL does not draw at all: a glob VALUE in container
position IS the glob's slot, a glob REF is a fatal.

    use strict; use warnings;
    our @gl = (5,6);
    my $gv = *main::gl;        # a glob VALUE
    my $gr = \*main::gl;       # a glob REF

                        perl 5.40.3            PCL (both trees)
    @{*main::gl}        2                      2                     ok
    @$gv                2                      2                     ok
    @$gr                Not an ARRAY reference 2                     WRONG
    $$gv[0]             5                      undef                 WRONG
    $$gr[0]             Not an ARRAY reference undef                 WRONG
    %$gv                0                      0                     ok
    %$gr                Not a HASH reference   0                     WRONG
    $$gv{q}             undef                  <gethash3 HOST ERROR> WRONG
    $$gr{q}             Not a HASH reference   <gethash3 HOST ERROR> WRONG
    *{$gr}{ARRAY}       2                      2                     ok
    @{$gr}              Not an ARRAY reference 2                     WRONG
    $gr->[0]            Not an ARRAY reference undef                 WRONG

TWO BUGS, one shared cause -- nothing at a container-deref site asks whether
the typeglob it is holding arrived as a VALUE or as a REFERENCE:

(a) THE GLOB-REF FATAL IS MISSING.  `%p-wrong-referent-p` deliberately
    excludes typeglobs and says why in its docstring: a glob VALUE in
    container position is perl's glob slot, which `p-cast-@` / `p-cast-%`
    implement (the `((p-typeglob-p v) (%p-glob-slot-place v â¦))` arm).  That
    exclusion is right for the VALUE and wrong for the REF.

(b) THE GLOB-VALUE ELEMENT PATH DOES NOT EXIST.  `p-aref-deref` and
    `p-gethash-deref` have no typeglob arm at all, so `$$gv[0]` falls to
    `p-aref` on a p-typeglob (undef) and `$$gv{q}` reaches SBCL's GETHASH
    (a host error naming a P-TYPEGLOB -- the IR-host-leak family at run
    time).  Only the whole-aggregate casts know the glob slot.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ALREADY IN THE TREE and is decidable: `is-ref` on the
box holding the typeglob, which is exactly what `%p-glob-value-box-p` reads
(`(and (p-box-p b) (p-typeglob-p (p-box-value b)) (not (p-box-is-ref b)))`,
the #163/#316/#1308 rule -- p-backslash sets the flag on the wrapper and
box-set propagates it).  `ref($gv)` is "" and `ref($gr)` is GLOB in PCL
TODAY, so the information reaches the box model correctly; it is only the
six container-deref sites that never ask.

SHAPE OF THE FIX (not designed further): ONE predicate beside
%p-glob-value-box-p -- "this reference's referent is a TYPEGLOB" -- consumed
by the same six sites that already consult %p-scalar-referent-p
(`p-aref-deref`, `p-gethash-deref`, `p-ensure-arrayref`, `p-ensure-hashref`,
`p-cast-@`, `p-cast-%`), plus a typeglob arm on the two element accessors
routed through the existing `%p-glob-slot-place`.  Half (b) must land with
or before half (a): making the REF fatal while the VALUE still answers undef
leaves the pair inconsistent in the other direction.

RISK TO PROBE FIRST (the "probe the case it would BREAK" rule): PCL routes
filehandles and `*{$pkg}{CODE}`-style glob work through these sites.  `open
my $fh` stores a STREAM payload, not a typeglob, so it is not in the family;
but `\*STDOUT`, IO::Handle's `${*$self}{â¦}` idiom and Exporter's
`*{"${pkg}::$name"} = \&x` all pass typeglobs around and must be probed
before the fatal is switched on.  The bar is #1628's: ~10 probes vs perl,
guard rows in Pl/t/ref-to-ref-01.t, the full sweep (a `cl/` change is
invisible to corpus-diff) and the io/ + op/ companion legs.
SIZE: M.
subject: a GLOB REF in container position is not perl's fatal, and a glob VALUE's ELEMENT access is missing: `$$gr[0]` answers undef, `$$gr{k}` leaks a gethash3 error, `$$gv[0]` answers undef where perl says 5
